text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the combination of stridor worsening with neck flexion and vomiting after feeding is very suggestive. Given the age and symptoms, have there been any episodes of choking on food or milk, or any history of reflux? REQUEST TEST: Upper GI_Series, Laryngoscopy, Barium_Swallow.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Barium_Swallow - Compression of the esophagus and trachea consistent with a vascular ring; Chest_X-ray - Evidence of tracheal compression and a vascular ring suggestive of a double aortic arch; Echocardiogram - Confirmatory findings of a double aortic arch.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Double Aortic Arch causing a vascular ring. The combination of stridor worsening with neck flexion, recurrent vomiting after feeding, and imaging confirming a double aortic arch with tracheal compression is diagnostic. No further questions or tests are required.
